where: top of the page: heading and dedication
scan: printed p. 5 begins with the heading 'INTRODUCTION' and the italic dedication 'A Oscar Zariski et André Weil.', then 'Ce mémoire, et les nombreux autres ...'
tex: \section*{Introduction} and the dedication stand before \oldpage[I]{5} (intro-fr.tex ll. 1-7), so both fall outside page 5
note: The marker belongs before \section*{Introduction}, as at pp. 101 and 130. The 'old' string spans the page boundary: it is an exact, unique substring of intro-fr.tex ll. 1-7 (LF line endings; identical in source/ega1 and the r20 release), not of page_005.tex, which starts at the marker. Apply it as a file-level edit (apply_manual.py, region 'file'). \oldpage is a \marginpar, which is allowed in vertical mode before \section*.

where: plan of the treatise, chapter II
scan: '— II. — Étude globale élémentaire de quelques classes de morphismes.' with the numeral II in regular roman (not bold)
tex: --- \textbf{II}. & --- Étude globale élémentaire de quelques classes de morphismes.
note: The chapter numerals of the plan are printed in the text weight. Measured at 300 dpi, each capital I in them has a 6 px stem and about 240 dark pixels, the same as the sentence-initial 'Il' on pp. 7 and 9; the bold reference numeral of (II, 2.4.3) on p. 101 measures 8-9 px stems, and its two I's merge into one blob. The chapter numerals in the running text of pp. 7-9 (chap. II, III, IV, V, VI, IX; 'III, 4.9.3') measure the same regular weight, and the TeX sets those plain.
